svg.title: Alpha particles passing through gold atoms
svg.desc: An expanded view of the atoms in a gold foil, drawn as circles about 10^−10 m across with a dot at each center for the nucleus (much larger than scale). Most alpha particles pass straight through; one passing close to a nucleus is deflected, and one striking a nucleus nearly head on bounces back. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A smaller impact parameter produces stronger nuclear scattering
Classical point-nucleus model: cot(θ/2) = b/a, a = Zz k e²/(2K∞). Dots use equal elapsed model time
along Coulomb hyperbolas. Nuclear size is enlarged; electrons are omitted.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
